items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I met Gigi in the band, I met Benny Golson in the band, Monk Montgomery, James Cleveland, Alan Dawson, good people in the band.

ctx.x: He was a fine guy. He was straight ahead. I spoke to him on the telephone sometime. He seems to be the same guy. Of course, he’s in another atmosphere now [laughs]. But, he’s still Quincy. He’s not like Mr. Jones, not that kind of stuff. I met Gigi in the band, I met Benny Golson in the band, Monk Montgomery, James Cleveland, Alan Dawson, good people in the band. That was a good time too. It was nice to meet these guys. We were like a family. Big bands usually develop cliques, so there were two cliques in this…
You mentioned your first recorded composition was “Farmer’s Market.” Had you already started writing before this? Had you started composing?

items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: in the trumpet section it was Art Farmer, there was Quincy Jones, there was Al Williams, there was The Whistler.

ctx.x: And so, the next day...I made it through that night. The next day we had...there was a message for everybody to meet in the lobby. I had been understood when I got there, the road manager said, everybody was going to meet in the lobby because we're leaving that day to go to Oregon. And everybody came down with their stuff and I had my bass and my bag, and I was trying to be hip.

Hip, I mean saying the right things. And I was speaking to different ones, saying 'Hey, oh yeah, don't I remember you, yeah, man, this is Wes's brother, yeah, hey man.' The cats... so and so...and we went through the thing with...There was Jimmy Cleveland, Quincy Jones and Art Farmer. You know, the cats. Just like I couldn't imagine. Then I begin to get afraid. The kid had come down, now.
